title: One definition, please
description:
This program is split across three `.cpp` files that all include `ids.h`. Each file compiles on its own without complaint. Then the **linker** refuses to join them: the header *defines* a variable and a function, so every `.cpp` that includes it gets its own copy, and the One Definition Rule allows only one.

Fix `ids.h` so the program links and prints `1 2 3`. Change only the header.

There are two quick fixes that look similar. One gives the whole program a single shared counter. The other quietly gives every `.cpp` file a private counter of its own, and the program prints `1 1 1`.
hints: `inline` on a function or variable means "this definition may appear in several files; they are all the same one". `static` means "each file gets its own".
lessonTitle: Name Lookup, ADL, Inline Namespaces and the ODR
